message:
fix(directory): 65537 was becoming port 1, and nothing downstream noticed

The reply to the address probe is the host's own public port -- what gets
published, and what decides whether anyone can reach the machine. The reader
refused only zero. It had no upper bound, so 65537 came through the cast to
uint16_t as 1, and its regex took the digits in front of a '.', so 29181.5
read as 29181. Neither is a value anything downstream rejects: both are
plausible ports, and a host nobody can reach looks like a network fault
rather than a parse.

Now the whole thing is checked before any of it is stored -- exact integer,
1..65535, non-empty address -- and a refusal leaves the previous observation
alone for the next probe to replace. The source-address check is unchanged.

Reproduced the defect before fixing it, by reverting the guard and running
the new cases: 65537 published as 1.2.3.4:1, 65536 as :0, 29181.5 as :29181,
fourteen digits as :65535, and an empty address as :29181. Five red, then
green. Without that step these would have been assertions that passed
before the change as well.

Three clients, two parsers: the viewer and the phone share
directory_rendezvous.cpp -- the Android build compiles that same file. That
one already had the range check, so what is new there is the fractional case
and an int overflow that was undefined rather than merely wrong. Said
plainly in the history entry, because "fixed in all three" would be doing
more work in the telling than in the code.

Also corrected: the combination table said an old client always ends up at
444. It does not. On http the +1 is the documented behaviour and works; an
old parser refuses https outright rather than dialling anything; and a new
server advertising a port that is not http+1 leaves an old client sending
observations somewhere nothing is listening, which the server then answers
with 409. The failure has a different shape in every cell.
